description.value: Participants performed spatial-perceptual tasks and received informative or confirmatory feedback while their brain activity was recorded.

spans.text: Fourteen male undergraduates performed a series of spatial-perceptual tasks and received feedback while their brain activity was recorded.
We used a mixed block/event-related design composed of three runs in total.
For informative feedback, task-relevant information was presented on the right side of the screen.
For informative feedback, task-relevant information was presented on the right side of the screen.

description.value: Feedback containing task-relevant information about the criterion missed.

spans.text: In these trials, when participants failed a trial, participants were informed about the criterion that they had missed (the size, the angle, or the response time).
For confirmatory feedback, a crosshair was displayed on the right side of the screen regardless of whether the answer was correct or not.
For confirmatory feedback, a crosshair was displayed on the right side of the screen regardless of whether the answer was correct or not.

description.value: Feedback indicating whether the answer was correct or incorrect without task-relevant information.

presentation_software.value: E-PRIME version 1.1; operating system not reported.

spans.text: Behavioral data were collected using E-PRIME v. 1.1.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to select one of three geometric figures by pressing the corresponding keyboard button. A response was correct only if the selected figure was largest in size, had the largest cut-off angle, and was made faster than the average response time from an undergraduate database.

stimuli.value: Three geometric figures, followed by feedback consisting of facial expressions and verbal statements; informative trials additionally displayed the missed criterion, whereas confirmatory trials displayed a crosshair.
